newsitem.title: UK: Citadel rises to premium on AIM debut.
newsitem.headline: Citadel rises to premium on AIM debut.

text.p: Shares in property group Citadel Holdings Plc on Wednesday rose to a 6.5 percent premium on their first day of dealings on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM), dealers said.
Citadel shares, issued at 100p, gained 6-1/2p to 106-1/2p by 1350 GMT.
Dealers estimated volume to be around 200,000 shares and said they had seen buying interest from private investors.
Citadel was formed by CLS Holdings Plc to invest mainly in office buildings in Paris and Lyon where the company believes prices have reached a low point in their cycle.

The company said the availability of favourable financing terms in France coupled with property price weakness, had presented Citadel with an opportunity to provide investors with an above average return.
Citadel raised about 33 million stg from a placing, which was effectively its market capitalisation at the issue price.
